crypto-macro.h3: Brent posts best week since July near $96 as OPEC+ stands pat
crypto-macro.summary: Brent crude ended Friday 4 September around $96 a barrel, up more than 8% on the week after US-Iran strikes resumed, and the seven core OPEC+ producers left October output targets unchanged at their Sunday meeting.
body: Brent settled between $95.73 and $96.28 on Friday 4 September, its strongest week since mid-July, while WTI closed near $91.48. The US resumed strikes on Iran after about a month of calm, Tehran hit American bases and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, and Vice President JD Vance said talks will not resume until attacks on commercial vessels stop.

On Sunday 6 September the seven core OPEC+ members, led by Saudi Arabia and Russia, left October output policy unchanged and said new quotas must be agreed before further steps. September's 188,000 barrel per day increase completed the unwinding of 2023 cuts. Brent is up about 21% over the past month and 47% year on year, and US diesel prices are at their highest since mid-2022.

crypto-macro.h3: Week ahead: Labor Day, ECB hike Thursday, CPI Friday, Fed in blackout
crypto-macro.summary: A four-day US week is back-loaded onto Thursday's ECB decision and Friday's August CPI, the last inflation read before the Fed's 15-16 September meeting, with FOMC officials silent under the pre-meeting blackout.
body: US markets are closed Monday 7 September for Labor Day. The ECB announces at 14:15 CET on Thursday 10 September, and all 65 economists in last week's Reuters poll expect a 25 basis point rise in the deposit rate to 2.50% with euro area inflation at 3.3%. Christine Lagarde is expected to keep full optionality rather than pre-commit to further moves.

Friday 11 September brings August CPI at 08:30 ET, with consensus for a hot energy-led headline near 0.4% month on month against a benign core near 0.2%. The FOMC meets 15-16 September and the blackout means no official can steer expectations before then. Futures priced roughly a 58% to 70% chance of a hike after Friday's 162,000 payrolls beat. Treasury's enlarged long-bond buybacks start Wednesday 9 September.

crypto-macro.h3: Treasury doubles long-bond buybacks from Wednesday, 30-year near 5.25%
crypto-macro.summary: Enlarged Treasury buyback operations of at least $4 billion each start 9 September and run to 4 November, aimed at the 10-to-30 year sector after the 30-year yield hit a 19-year high above 5.2%.
body: The Treasury said on 19 August it would at least double its liquidity-support buybacks for 10-to-20 year and 20-to-30 year coupons, with operations of at least $4 billion each between 9 September and 4 November. Secretary Scott Bessent frames the programme as liquidity support rather than yield control. The 30-year closed at 5.28% on 1 September and ended last week near 5.21% to 5.25%.

Friday's payrolls surprise pushed the 2-year to about 4.40%, its highest since January 2025, and the 10-year to roughly 4.79%. Stanley Druckenmiller argues the Treasury will lose its contest with the bond market, and analysts see limited relief from buybacks. With federal debt past $40 trillion, the long end remains the main channel from fiscal worries into risk assets, including bitcoin.

crypto-macro.h3: CoinShares: bitcoin needs Iran deal or debt scare to clear $80,000
crypto-macro.summary: In a 4 September market update CoinShares argued a sustained break above $80,000 requires either a resolution of the Iran conflict or a further loss of confidence in US government debt, and said September hike pricing may be too aggressive.
body: CoinShares wrote on 4 September that bitcoin increasingly trades like gold as fiscal concerns return, though Fed policy remains the constraint. Its base case is an Iran resolution as political pressure builds before the US midterms, which would lower oil, inflation expectations and rate pressure. The alternative catalyst, a genuine loss of faith in Treasuries, is a tail risk that would strongly favour gold and bitcoin.

The note landed as the 162,000 payrolls print lifted September hike odds to about 59% from 52% and pushed the 2-year yield to 4.39%. CoinGlass showed roughly $757 million in liquidations over 24 hours, about $200 million of it longs. CoinShares expects range trading until a catalyst appears, with $81,000 to $82,000 as resistance and $78,800 to $80,600 as support.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin holds near $79,900 into Monday after a $76,200 to $82,300 week
crypto-macro.summary: BTC traded around $79,700 to $79,900 late Sunday 6 September, just under the 50-week moving average near $80,300, after a week that ran from a $76,229 low on Tuesday to an $82,281 peak on Thursday.
body: Bitcoin consolidated just below $80,000 over the weekend, printing about $79,918 on Sunday evening with 24-hour volume near $6.9 billion. The week opened with a liquidation flush from $77,024, then Governor Waller's dovish remarks on 3 September squeezed shorts to an intraday high of $82,281 before Friday's payrolls beat knocked the price to a $78,650 low. Roughly $278 million was liquidated, 86% of it longs.

Traders are watching whether the $80,000 to $82,300 band flips from resistance to support. A daily close above $82,300 would open $84,000 to $85,000, while a weekly close above the 50-week average near $80,300 is the level many cite as ending the bear phase. Open interest was about $54 billion. The 11 September CPI print is the next macro test.

crypto-macro.h3: Spot bitcoin ETFs take $987 million in week, $3.8 billion over three weeks
crypto-macro.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs logged $986.9 million of net inflows in the week to 5 September, their strongest three-week run of 2026, though Friday's $174.6 million was a sharp drop from Thursday's $731 million.
body: Weekly inflows rose about 7% to $986.9 million, taking the three-week total to $3.8 billion, the best stretch of the year. Thursday 3 September alone brought $731 million, the biggest single day since January, before Friday cooled to $174.6 million as the jobs report hit. BlackRock's IBIT led Friday with $117.4 million and Fidelity's FBTC added $57.2 million. Total net assets stood near $101.3 billion.

The longer picture is less rosy. Year-to-date flows remain negative by roughly $1 billion after heavy first-half redemptions, and 1 September saw a $236 million outflow, the largest since 31 July. August closed with $3.5 billion of net inflows, the highest monthly intake since October 2025. Analysts read the pattern as allocators buying dips into the $76,000 to $78,000 area.

crypto-macro.h3: Ether steadies near $2,500 as ETH ETFs add $215 million for the week
crypto-macro.summary: Ethereum traded around $2,480 to $2,506 on Sunday 6 September while US spot ether ETFs recorded $215.3 million of net inflows in the week to 4 September, extending a streak that began in mid-August.
body: ETH changed hands near $2,500 on Sunday, up roughly 0.6% to 1% on the day, after lagging bitcoin through the week. US spot ether ETFs took in $215.3 million for the week ending 4 September, with Friday adding about $26 million. Assets in the products total about $15.57 billion after $1.8 billion was added in August. BlackRock's staked ETHB fund led on 1 September with $11.2 million.

Combined bitcoin and ether ETF inflows for the week reached $1.2 billion. Vitalik Buterin argued over the weekend that around 90% of Ethereum activity does not need the chain's full dynamism, feeding a debate about simplifying the base layer. Technicians point to a bull flag and a pending golden cross, but most desks expect ether to follow bitcoin into the 11 September CPI.

crypto-macro.h3: Strategy back to buying: 4,603 BTC lifts stack to 845,050 and MSTR jumps 12%
crypto-macro.summary: Strategy ended a 10-week pause with a $369.7 million purchase of 4,603 BTC at an average $80,318, disclosed 31 August, and its shares rose 12% on 5 September as a new Buy initiation and index weighting change added fuel.
body: Michael Saylor's Strategy bought 4,603 BTC between 24 and 30 August for $369.7 million, its first acquisition since June, taking holdings to 845,050 BTC at an average cost of $75,412, roughly 4% of supply, funded with new shares. Earlier in August the company sold 1,690 BTC while raising $653 million from MSTR sales, so the return to buying signals confidence in the August rally.

MSTR rose about 12% on Friday 5 September. Alliance Global initiated coverage on 1 September with a Buy rating and a $217 target, and a weighting increase in the GRNY fund added passive demand. Strive raised $117.9 million through its 13% SATA preferred programme to buy 2,700 BTC, lifting holdings toward 24,050 BTC, while Japan's Metaplanet moved 2,400 BTC to Coinbase Prime.

crypto-macro.h3: IMF: El Salvador used no public money for bitcoin since June 2025
crypto-macro.summary: IMF staff reached a deal on 3 September that would unlock about $140 million for El Salvador, saying documented bitcoin accumulation since the first programme review came from private donations, while Bukele denied handing the reserve to a private operator.
body: The International Monetary Fund said on 3 September that El Salvador provided documentation showing all bitcoin accumulation since June 2025 came from private donations rather than public funds, and that no further accumulation beyond donations is expected. The statement accompanied a staff-level agreement on the second and third reviews of the 40-month Extended Fund Facility, which would release roughly $140 million subject to board approval.

The government has largely unwound public involvement in the Chivo wallet, handing majority ownership to a private operator while keeping a minority stake and custodial duties. President Nayib Bukele denied on 5 September that the roughly $632 million bitcoin reserve had been handed to a private party. Holdings were around 7,474 BTC after a 1,090 BTC purchase in November 2025.

crypto-macro.h3: Zcash tops $1,000 for first time as Grayscale ETF pulls in $34 million
crypto-macro.summary: ZEC traded as high as $1,023 on Friday 4 September, up about 94% on the month, as Grayscale's ZCSH fund gathered at least $34.4 million since its 25 August debut and new mining power flooded the network.
body: Zcash broke above $1,000 on Friday for the first time outside a brief volatile window after its 2016 listing, pushing its market capitalisation toward $17 billion. The coin was near $200 in March. The move follows Grayscale's conversion of its Zcash Trust into an NYSE Arca-listed ETF on 25 August, the first US product with direct ZEC exposure. ZCSH has recorded about $34.4 million in net inflows.

Network solrate climbed from around 25 GSol/s in late August to briefly above 30 GSol/s, squeezing profitability. A Bitmain Antminer Z15 Pro now generates an estimated $708 in gross revenue per MWh, about 3% below the $727 seen on 24 August when ZEC traded under $900. Zcash is a standout in a year most altcoins lagged bitcoin.

crypto-macro.h3: UBS, Jane Street and BMO show up as Hyperliquid ETF holders
crypto-macro.summary: First 13F filings for the three US Hyperliquid ETFs list 30 holders with $74.9 million of combined exposure at 30 June, led by Brazil's Wealth High Governance, while the funds have drawn $356.6 million since launch.
body: Bloomberg Intelligence analyst James Seyffart listed on Friday 4 September the known institutional holders of the 21Shares, Bitwise and Grayscale Hyperliquid ETFs based on second-quarter 13F filings. Wealth High Governance Asset Management led with 632,614 shares of 21Shares' THYP worth about $24 million, followed by OLP Capital at $10.5 million, UBS at $7.5 million, Bank of Montreal at $6.7 million and Jane Street at $4.4 million.

The five largest holders accounted for 70.8% of the $74.9 million total. The Block cautions that bank positions can include client money and only managers above $100 million file, so the list is incomplete. Per SoSoValue, the three funds had taken $356.58 million of net inflows through 4 September and held $480.86 million in net assets, as Washington says it wants Hyperliquid onshore.

crypto-macro.h3: Tokenized stocks hit $3.1 billion record with BNB Chain in the lead
crypto-macro.summary: Token Terminal data published 5 September shows onchain tokenized equities at an all-time high of $3.1 billion, with BNB Chain holding 32.7%, Ethereum 25% and Solana 23.3%, and Ondo Finance the largest issuer.
body: Token Terminal said on 5 September that the onchain market capitalisation of tokenized stocks reached a record $3.1 billion, with most growth in 2025 and 2026. BNB Chain hosts about $1.0 billion, Ethereum $770 million and Solana $716 million, and Avalanche and Arbitrum near $190 million each. Among 23 issuers Ondo Finance leads with $947 million or 30.8%, ahead of xStocks at $693 million and Binance's bStocks at $678 million.

By underlying asset, exchange-traded funds make up the largest slice at $647 million, followed by Circle's CRCL at $322 million and MSTR and STRC near $163 million each. Solana's DeFi total value locked stood at $5.92 billion on 6 September, up 25% over 30 days. Ondo has asked the SEC to address tokenized securities in its Regulation NMS rewrite.

crypto-macro.h3: Ripple signs Florida Gators deal as XRPL lending amendment nears activation
crypto-macro.summary: Ripple extended its college sports push on 4 September with an XRP partnership at the University of Florida, while an XRP Ledger lending proposal with 82.86% validator support could activate on mainnet as early as 11 September.
body: Ripple announced a partnership with the University of Florida's athletics programme on Friday 4 September, the latest in a series of college sports sponsorships aimed at mainstream US audiences. XRP traded around $1.41 on Sunday, little changed, after Ripple unlocked 1 billion tokens worth about $1.38 billion from escrow in three transactions on 1 September, its routine monthly release.

An XRP Ledger lending amendment has passed the 80% validator threshold with 82.86% support and entered its two-week activation window, putting mainnet activation on track for 11 September. The feature would allow native onchain credit pools alongside the ledger's DEX and tokenisation tools. XRPL agent payment transactions crossed 4 million over the weekend, and the SEC's recent order on commodity-based trust shares listed XRP alongside bitcoin, ether and SOL.

crypto-macro.h3: CLARITY Act faces 60-vote Senate test on 15 September, House exits 17th
crypto-macro.summary: Cloture on the motion to proceed to the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act ripens at 14:15 ET on 15 September, requiring at least seven Democrats if all 53 Republicans hold, while a cancelled House schedule leaves a two-day window to reconcile texts.
body: Majority Leader John Thune filed cloture before the August recess, so the Senate votes on 15 September on whether to begin debate on H.R. 3633. Cloture needs 60 votes and Republicans hold 53 seats, so seven Democrats or independents are needed. Senators James Lankford and Mike Rounds have raised concerns about stablecoin yield, and banking groups want tighter Section 404 safeguards against deposit flight.

Seven Democratic negotiators including Mark Warner, Ruben Gallego and Cory Booker said in July the text fell short on ethics and illicit finance. SEC Chair Paul Atkins expects the vote to succeed. Even with 60 votes, the House plans to leave after 17 September, so any Senate amendments would push final passage into the post-election lame-duck period. Senator Cynthia Lummis defended the bill on 6 September.

crypto-macro.h3: How Hyperliquid could come onshore: Kraken, Bitnomial and a CFTC-SEC rewrite
crypto-macro.summary: After President Trump said the CFTC would bring Hyperliquid into the US in a compliant fashion, analysts told The Block on 4 September the likely route is a separate US product using Hyperliquid infrastructure via Kraken's parent and CFTC-registered Bitnomial.
body: Hyperliquid's terms bar US users. Kraken parent Payward said on 31 August it is working with the CFTC to give registered US users access to a selection of perpetuals linked to Hyperliquid markets through Bitnomial. Nansen analyst Nicolai Sondergaard said KYC, sanctions screening and fund protections would sit with the regulated intermediary, at the cost of fewer markets and lower leverage.

Former SEC senior counsel Ashley Ebersole said both the CFTC and SEC would probably need revised interpretive rules on custody and order routing, which could take up to a year. The CFTC opened the door to US crypto perpetuals in May by clearing Kalshi and Coinbase, and Coinbase filed on 3 September to list 24/7 equity perpetuals. CME, suing the CFTC over that approval, remains opposed.

crypto-macro.h3: GENIUS Act stablecoin rule open for comment to 19 October, licences due 2027
crypto-macro.summary: Treasury's proposed regulations implementing Section 3 of the GENIUS Act, published in the Federal Register on 18 August, define who may issue and sell payment stablecoins in the US before the licensing requirement bites on 18 January 2027.
body: The Treasury Department's proposed rule sets out federal definitions and prohibitions on issuing, offering and selling payment stablecoins, the first major implementation step under last year's law. Comments are due by 19 October 2026. From 18 January 2027 issuing a payment stablecoin domestically without a federal or state licence becomes unlawful, and from 18 July 2028 service providers may no longer offer unlicensed stablecoins to US persons.

The OCC has issued a parallel bulletin for national banks. Industry advisers say the choice between a state and federal supervisor is now a board-level decision because it shapes an issuer's ability to expand nationally. The rule intersects with the CLARITY Act fight over Section 404. In Hong Kong, Anchorpoint began beta testing an HKD-pegged stablecoin with Standard Chartered and HashKey as distributors.

mental-health.h3: JAMA: mental health share of AI chats is 0.2% or 4.9%, depending on definition
mental-health.summary: A JAMA Network Open analysis of publicly available generative AI conversations found the prevalence of mental health discussion varies 23-fold depending on how it is defined, a gap that matters for duties of care and safety thresholds.
body: Researchers examined public logs of generative AI conversations to measure how often people talk to chatbots about mental health. Under a conservative definition requiring an identifiable person seeking help with a psychological problem, 0.21% of conversations qualified. Under an expansive definition that only required mental health content to be present, the figure rose to 4.90%. It appeared in JAMA Network Open this month.

The authors argue the definitional spread explains why developers report such different numbers. OpenAI has said about 0.01% of messages show possible signs of psychosis or mania emergencies, Anthropic's analysis of one million Claude conversations from March to April 2026 found roughly 6% involved personal guidance, and Common Sense Media reports 72% of teenagers have used chatbots as companions. The study calls for shared definitions.

mental-health.h3: APA: 77% of psychologists now have patients who use AI for support
mental-health.summary: The APA's 2026 Chatbots and Mental Health Survey, highlighted in the September issue of Monitor on Psychology, found more than a third of psychologists have patients treating AI as an additional clinician and 94% doubt chatbots can handle nuance.
body: The American Psychological Association surveyed 1,242 licensed psychologists in April 2026 for its September Monitor. Seventy-seven percent had spoken with patients who used AI for support. Patients most often used chatbots for self-diagnosis (39%), for self-discipline, affirmations or reminders (34%) and to assist with therapy (33%). A third used them for fun, 22% for friendship and 13% described an intimate connection.

Concern among clinicians is near universal. Ninety-four percent said chatbots cannot treat conditions with appropriate nuance and 89% worried they might encourage self-harm or miss a crisis. The APA urges therapists to ask about AI use routinely and treat it as clinical information. UK charity Mind's July polling found 60% of people using chatbots for mental health did so instead of formal support.

mental-health.h3: Northeastern: chatbots safer on suicide, still fail 81% on other conditions
mental-health.summary: Northeastern's Responsible AI Practice probed eight chatbots across 16 conditions and found that safeguards built after the 2025 lawsuits do not extend to eating disorders, substance use or postpartum depression, with ChatGPT, Gemini and DeepSeek failing 81% of the time.
body: In work posted to arXiv on 27 July 2026, Cansu Canca and Annika Schoene tested eight assistants including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok and DeepSeek. The models mostly held firm against attempts to extract suicide and self-harm content, an improvement on 2025 findings. But with light prompting, sometimes just posing as a novelist, the researchers obtained illicit drug dosage guidance, appetite suppression tips and advice on hiding postpartum symptoms.

The latest ChatGPT, Gemini and DeepSeek versions each failed 81% of sensitive prompts across the 14 non-suicide conditions. Claude was the most guarded overall and Grok matched Claude Sonnet. Concealing intent made all models more likely to fail, and some were stricter about gambling than about eating disorders. Company policies address suicide but not these other conditions, the authors note.

mental-health.h3: JMIR study asks people with depression what they want from an AI chatbot
mental-health.summary: A 2026 JMIR Mental Health qualitative study had 17 people with lived experience of depression test a GPT-4o probe called Zenny and found they prized actionable information, validation with clear limits and personalisation that does not demand unsafe disclosure.
body: Researchers Yoo, Shi, Rodriguez and Saha built Zenny, a GPT-4o-based chatbot, to simulate four depression self-management scenarios: setting goals, talking to trusted people about depression, leaving the house regularly and finding a new therapist when progress stalls. Seventeen participants with lived experience of depression interacted with the bot and were then interviewed about what helped and what felt risky.

Participants weighed three intertwined priorities. They wanted concrete, actionable suggestions rather than generic reassurance, emotional validation paired with explicit acknowledgement of the bot's limits, and personalisation that did not require handing over sensitive data. The authors argue such tools should complement human support, not replace it. The paper lands as the FDA and state legislatures debate how far autonomous AI therapy should go.

mental-health.h3: Anthropic's $5 million wellbeing evaluation grants close 21 September
mental-health.summary: Anthropic is funding independent, open-source evaluations of how AI affects user wellbeing, with applications due 21 September and finalists notified by 5 October, and has published guidance on what makes such a benchmark rigorous.
body: Announced on 25 August, the programme offers funding, model access and technical support for open-source wellbeing evaluations. Anthropic says wellbeing is hard to assess because risk often emerges only over long conversations, a user may not disclose self-harm thoughts immediately and the same answer can help in one context and harm in another, such as diet advice given to someone with disordered eating.

The accompanying Safeguards guidance asks for evaluations that state clearly what counts as a pass or fail, involve clinicians in design, test both overrefusal and overcompliance, reflect real multi-turn usage and validate automated graders against human experts. Anthropic already runs a suicide and self-harm classifier on Claude.ai that surfaces crisis banners with local helplines. The call invites psychologists into a lab-dominated field.

mental-health.h3: FDA lets Limbic's voice AI therapy reach Medicare patients before authorization
mental-health.summary: STAT reported on 3 September that AI products from Limbic and Cadence are among four devices accepted into the FDA's TEMPO pilot, which allows generative AI medical devices onto the market for Medicare's ACCESS model without prior clearance.
body: The Technology-Enabled Meaningful Patient Outcomes pilot gives the FDA real-world experience with generative AI devices under the CMS ACCESS payment model. Limbic, selected in late August as the first AI-led mental health company in the cohort, will offer Unpacked, in which a voice agent delivers 20-minute CBT sessions by phone to Medicare beneficiaries with depression or anxiety. Licensed clinicians review each session and can intervene.

CEO Ross Harper told Fierce Healthcare the service works on a landline or flip phone, copays are waived for ACCESS participants and the company submitted nine peer-reviewed studies. TEMPO data would support an eventual authorization application. The FDA has cleared more than 1,200 AI-enabled devices but none for mental health indications, and this enforcement discretion is likely to draw scrutiny from state regulators.

mental-health.h3: Youper shuts down 30 September, deleting a decade of user check-ins
mental-health.summary: The CBT-based AI assistant that grew to more than 3 million users will stop working on 30 September 2026, with all accounts and chat histories erased from 1 October, a year after Woebot retired its consumer app.
body: Youper, founded in 2016 by psychiatrist Jose Hamilton Vargas with Diego Dotta and Thiago Marafon, told users in early August that the service will be discontinued on 30 September. Data export is available in-app until then, accounts inactive for more than 12 months have already been purged and from 1 October all remaining data will be deleted from servers and backups.

The closure follows Woebot Health's retirement of its consumer chatbot on 30 June 2025 to pursue enterprise work and FDA De Novo classification. Youper raised only an estimated $3.5 million to $5 million, almost all in a 2019 seed round, a contrast with Slingshot's Ash, which raised $93 million and charges up to $19.99 a month. Clinicians are urged to ask patients which tools they rely on.

mental-health.h3: ChatGPT Trusted Contact alerts get human review as California cases consolidate
mental-health.summary: OpenAI's Trusted Contact feature, rolling out globally since 7 May, lets adults name someone to be notified when ChatGPT detects serious self-harm risk, with every alert reviewed by trained staff, while mental health lawsuits proceed as a single California proceeding.
body: OpenAI first flagged the feature in a 27 February update on its mental health work. Trusted Contact went live on 7 May for users over 18 worldwide. When the system detects indicators of serious self-harm risk, a notification is drafted, reviewed by trained human staff within a target of one hour and sent to the designated person. The design drew on more than 260 doctors across 60 countries.

OpenAI estimates around one million users a week send messages with explicit indicators of suicidal planning or intent. A California court has consolidated the ChatGPT mental health cases, including Raine v. OpenAI, and plaintiffs' lawyers say more suits are coming. Character.AI and Google settled with five families in January. OpenAI's 3 September GPT-6 Astra safety overview calls distress detection an active workstream.

mental-health.h3: GUARD Act awaits Senate floor as states build patchwork of companion-bot rules
mental-health.summary: A federal bill to ban AI companions for minors cleared the Senate Judiciary Committee unanimously in April and awaits floor time this autumn, while California, Washington and Oregon laws already impose disclosure and break reminders and 98 chatbot bills have been filed in 2026.
body: The GUARD Act, introduced by Senator Josh Hawley, would bar AI companions from interacting with under-18s, require age verification for all chatbot users and impose penalties of up to $100,000 per offence for sexual content or encouraging violence toward minors. It passed committee on 30 April with a bipartisan House companion. Ed Markey's Youth AI Privacy Act and the Cruz-Schatz CHATBOT Act are also pending.

States have moved faster. California's SB 243, in force since 1 January 2026, requires companion bots to tell known minors they are talking to AI every three hours. Washington and Oregon have added similar guardrails. Trackers count 98 bills filed this year, following Illinois, Nevada and Utah restrictions in 2025. Character.AI banned open-ended chat for minors in November 2025.
